sources.entry: Audacity - Free, open source, cross-platform audio software

summary.one_liner: Audacity is a free, open source, cross-platform multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other systems.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Audacity as an easy-to-use multi-track audio editor and recorder. It runs on Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. The README is short and does not list specific editing features, file formats or plugins. It states that the master branch is being restructured for Audacity 4, which brings a new UI and refactoring, while Audacity 3.x patches go to the audacity3 branch. It points to separate build instructions for 3.x and 4 and to YouTube, Discord and a blog for updates. Licensing is GPLv3, with most code under GPLv2-or-later and exceptions for third-party libraries in /au3/lib-src and VST3-related code.
use_cases: contribute patches to an open source audio editor
use a free audio editor on Windows, macOS or Linux
how_to_run: See the build instructions for Audacity 3.x (audacity3 branch) linked from the README
See the separate build instructions for Audacity 4 linked from the README
stack: C++ (inferred from the au3 source directory name only; not stated in README)
notable: Multi-track audio editing and recording for Windows, macOS and GNU/Linux
Audacity 4 is under development with an entirely new UI
Active 3.x line maintained on the audacity3 branch for contributions
caveats: The master branch is undergoing major structural change and is not currently friendly to new contributors
Contributors must branch off audacity3 for 3.x patches
